Query a remote DuckDB server as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__duckdb.R
oauth_db_duckdb.Rd

Query a shared remote DuckDB database with each visitor's access token. Quack connects your R client to the server, which checks the token and controls data access. You can query its tables with DBI or dbplyr.

Usage

oauth_db_duckdb(
  authorization,
  host,
  port = 9494L,
  schema = "main",
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  allow_local_http = FALSE,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

host

One TCP hostname or address. Enclose IPv6 addresses in brackets.

port

Quack server or TLS proxy port, default 9494.

schema

Default schema in the remote database, default "main".

ca_bundle

Optional CA certificate bundle path for a private server CA.

allow_local_http

Allow unencrypted HTTP for localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]. Defaults to FALSE; use only for local development.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, usually named con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression, then pass the connection to DBI. Before sign-in, the function waits quietly.

Details

Install duckdb 1.5.3 or later and matching quack and httpfs extensions before starting the app. Configure the remote server's OAuth validator, trusted issuer, audience and data permissions. A local DuckDB file doesn't provide user sign-in.

Create the helper inside server() and call con() before each query. Connections require verified TLS unless you explicitly allow HTTP for local development with allow_local_http.

The helper selects the remote catalog oauth_remote and your chosen schema for table queries. Standalone expressions can still run locally; query a remote table to check server access.

Token renewal replaces the connection and ends any transaction on it. Keep transactions within one operation. Sign-out, account changes or session end close the connection. The helper doesn't replay failed SQL.

See also

vignette("duckdb", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has server requirements, sign-in setup and a complete app. oauth_db_demo() runs a local Quack and Keycloak example.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Inside server(), using a client for the Quack server's issuer and audience:
con <- oauth_db_duckdb(
  auth$connection, host = "duckdb.example.org", port = 443,
  required_scopes = "quack:read"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT * FROM orders LIMIT 20")
})
} # }
